title: #16 D-099: the group chain counts dag.json's group_after edges (group A after group B)
objective: core/chain.py orders the groups by ticket dependencies plus dag.json's `group_after` edges between groups that are not landed or cancelled, so every reader of the chain (the controller's regression gate, idle and stuck pages, the board's DAG view, and the cycle checks of `actl dag` and the opener) follows those edges.
outline: devloop/core/chain.py: waits(snap): after the ticket loop, read (snap.raw.get('dag') or {}).get('group_after'); when it is a dict, for each key A that is a str and whose value is a list, for each element B that is a str, add B to out[A] when A and B are in `live` and A != B. A small public helper that returns the well-formed edges {A: [B, ...]} (all of them, not only live ones; suggested name after_edges(snap)) is welcome: the later `actl dag after` ticket may reuse it. Do NOT name any helper, variable or key `group_order` (or `_gnum`, or slice-and-int a group id): test_chain.DagOrderUnits.test_no_code_sorts_groups_by_the_digits_of_the_id fails on any devloop line containing those. Keep order()'s algorithm (place each group after every group it waits for, pulled ahead recursively, by created key then natural id); do not switch to a Kahn order (acceptance 2 pins the difference). Update the module docstring's 'Group B waits for group A when ...' paragraph. devloop/README.md: one or two sentences inside the 'Groups form one chain' paragraph. No change is expected in core/dagedit.py, ticket_creator.py, board.py, ticket_controller.py or tickets.py: they read the chain through these functions (dagedit.check and group_problems run chain.cycle on a deep copy of snap.raw, which holds group_after); if one needs a change, say why in the hand-in.
test_plan: Verifier: one case each for acceptance 2, 3, 4, 6(a), 6(b), 7(a), 7(b), 8 and 9, in a new class T<this ticket's id>Acceptance(LoopCase) in tests_devloop/test_chain.py between class BehindLine and class DagOrderUnits. setUp pops every DEVLOOP_* key from self.env (as T122Acceptance.setUp does). Pure cases (2, 3, 4, 6b, 7a, 7b) build core.pool.Snapshot({'dag': {'tickets': {...}, 'group_after': {...}}, 'tickets': {...}, 'groups': {gid: {'id', 'state', 'members', 'created'}}, 'inbox': {}, 'lessons': {}, 'memory_state': {}}) directly and import inside the case: `from core import chain`, `import board`, `import ticket_controller`, `import ticket_creator`. Pool cases (6a, 8): tickets with self.add(N, group='gN', target='int/gN', ...), groups with self.pool.update(lambda tx: tx.put_group({...})), and dag.json's edge with self.pool.update(lambda tx: tx.put_dag(dict(tx.data.raw['dag'], group_after={...})), 'test: edge') written AFTER every self.add() (the harness's add rewrites dag.json with only 'tickets' until the sibling ticket on that lands). 6(a) runs self.run_py('dag_edit.py', 'dep', '1', '--add', '2', '--reason', 'r'); 8 runs self.controller() (about 3 s measured) and reads 'regression started' / 'landed' rows from the groups' history, as T122Acceptance.test_a_ticket_depending_on_a_later_group_lands_in_its_own_group does. Case 9 reads devloop/README.md split on blank lines and the paragraph starting 'Groups form one chain': assert it contains 'group_after' and 'D-099'. Expected values come from this ticket. Measured by the opener on 22af64f in a scratch clone: equivalent cases for 2, 3, 4, 6a, 6b, 7a, 7b and 8 all fail today (8: g1 lands first), and pass with a 7-line trial change of waits(), with test_chain and test_dag_edit still green (34 s for all three modules). Implementer: acceptance 1 and 5 in its own unit tests in a new class (e.g. GroupAfterUnits(unittest.TestCase)) in tests_devloop/test_chain.py between class T117Acceptance and class BehindLine; run `python3 devloop/run_tests.py test_chain test_dag_edit` (about 35 s).
notes: Group g11: the open group of the GitHub issue #16 follow-ups (D-097, D-098); D-099 is the third ruling from the same incident. File overlap with g11 is small: #134 may add a predicate to core/chain.py (a new function, not waits()) and #135 edits the README paragraph before 'Groups form one chain' (keep the edit inside 'Groups form one chain' so the hunks stay apart). 'Pool validation refuses a dag.json whose group edges make a cycle' (request item 5) is met here: there is no separate dag.json validator; every writer validates inside its one pool write through chain.cycle (dagedit.check for `actl dag dep/move` and the reviser's dag part, ticket_creator.group_problems for the opener, and `actl dag after` from the later ticket), so counting edges in waits() makes all of them refuse a cycle through an edge. Deliberately no check inside core/pool.py Tx.put_dag: a raise there comes after other files of the transaction were written, and a pool transaction has no rollback.
acceptance: 1 (data shape, fixed for every later ticket and test): dag.json may hold a top-level key `group_after` next to `tickets`: an object mapping a group id A to a list of group ids B, meaning 'A comes after each B'. In a core.pool Snapshot it is snap.raw['dag']['group_after']. core/chain.py waits(snap) adds B to A's waits-for set for each listed B when A and B are both groups of the snapshot whose state is not landed or cancelled, both are strings and A != B; the ticket-dependency part of waits() is unchanged. order(), sequence(), cycle(), holds(), waits_for(), behind(), behind_line() and with_behind() keep their algorithm and signatures and see the edges only through waits().

2 (today's tie-break, pull-ahead): Snapshot with groups g1, g2, g3 all open, created '2026-11-20T00:00:01Z', '...02Z', '...03Z', no tickets, group_after {'g1': ['g3']}: chain.order(snap) == ['g3', 'g1', 'g2'], chain.waits_for(snap, 'g1') == 'g3', chain.behind(snap, 'g3') == ['g1', 'g2']. (A Kahn-style smallest-key-first order would give ['g2', 'g3', 'g1']; that is wrong here.)

3 (edges to or from a landed, cancelled or unknown group order nothing): groups g1 open (created ...01Z), g2 open (...02Z), g3 landed (...03Z), g4 cancelled (...04Z), g5 open (...05Z), no tickets, group_after {'g1': ['g3', 'g4', 'g5'], 'g9': ['g1']} (g9 is no group): chain.order(snap) == ['g5', 'g1', 'g2'] and chain.sequence(snap) == ['g3', 'g4', 'g5', 'g1', 'g2']; the edges stay in the data untouched.

4 (a cycle through a ticket dependency and an edge): groups g1 (...01Z) and g2 (...02Z) open; ticket '1' ready in g1 with depends_on ['2'], ticket '2' ready in g2; group_after {'g2': ['g1']}: chain.cycle(snap) == ['g1', 'g2', 'g1'], and chain.order(snap) does not raise and sorted(chain.order(snap)) == ['g1', 'g2'].

5 (hand edits never raise): with groups g1 (...01Z) and g2 (...02Z) open and no tickets, each of group_after = ['g1'], 'g1', {'g2': 'g1'}, {'g2': [1, None, ['g1'], {'g1': 1}]}, {'g2': {'g1': 1}} gives chain.order(snap) == ['g1', 'g2'] and chain.cycle(snap) is None (non-string or unhashable entries are skipped, never looked up in a set).

6 (the existing cycle checks count edges; no change expected in those files): (a) pool with groups g1 {#1} and g2 {#2} open (same created stamp), #1 and #2 ready without deps, and dag.json group_after {'g2': ['g1']}: `python3 devloop/dag_edit.py dep 1 --add 2 --reason r` exits 2 with exactly one stderr line containing 'the group order would be a cycle: g1 -> g2 -> g1', pool HEAD unchanged; (b) ticket_creator.group_problems(result, snap) on a Snapshot with the groups, tickets and edge of item 4 minus #1's dependency (#1 with depends_on []) and result {'tickets': [{'key': 'new-1'}], 'dag': {'new-1': {'depends_on': ['2'], 'group': 'g1'}}} == ['new-1: group g1 makes the group order a cycle: g1 -> g2 -> g1'].

7 (what people read follows the edges): (a) groups g1, g2, g3 open (...01Z, ...02Z, ...03Z), tickets '1' in g1, '2' in g2, '3' in g3 (ready, no deps), group_after {'g1': ['g3']}: [gid for gid, _ in board.dag_lanes(snap, {'1', '2', '3'})] == ['g3', 'g1', 'g2']; (b) groups g1 pr (...01Z) with ticket '1' merged, g2 open (...02Z) with '2' ready, g3 open (...03Z) with '3' ready, no deps, group_after {'g1': ['g3']}: ticket_controller.idle_lines(snap) contains 'g1 waits for g3 to land (place 2 in the chain)' and 'g2 waits for g1 to land (place 3 in the chain)'.

8 (end to end, the controller's gate and D-098): pool with ticket 1 (needs_verifier False, group 'g1', target 'int/g1') and ticket 2 (needs_verifier False, group 'g2', target 'int/g2'), group records g1 created '2026-11-23T00:00:01Z' and g2 created '2026-11-23T00:00:02Z' (open, branch 'int/gN', members ['N'], fix_round 0, job None, one history row), then dag.json group_after {'g1': ['g2']}; one controller run exits 0 and: both tickets landed; g1 has exactly one 'regression started' event, at or after g2's last 'landed' event; g1's events contain 'main moved to <g2's landed_sha[:12]>: merged it into int/g1' before 'regression started'; dag.json's group_after is still {'g1': ['g2']} afterwards (an edge to a landed group stays as history).

9 (docs): the core/chain.py module docstring and the devloop/README.md paragraph that starts with 'Groups form one chain' say that group B also waits for group A when dag.json's `group_after` lists A under B (D-099), while neither group is landed or cancelled, and that such an edge to a landed or cancelled group stays in dag.json but orders nothing. The README sentence goes inside that paragraph (no blank line added): test_groups.DagEditUnits.test_item8_docs reads the paragraph right after it and must keep passing unchanged.

vision: 目的與成功指標: 每張票需要我介入幾次 and 等我處理的事積了多少 (down): in T the owner's order for g63, g70, g78 behind #320's group could not be expressed at all; with this and `actl dag after` it is one command instead of a hand edit of the pool or cancelling and reopening three groups (inferred, not measured).
removes: the main session's inability to order a group behind another when the group's tickets are merged (no ticket dependency can be added any more, D-089): the order no longer comes only from ticket dependencies and creation time; no new gate - the existing chain gate reads the edges.
request:
# `actl dag` can change the order of groups (docs/DECISIONS.md D-099; follow-up of GitHub issue #16)

The user's ruling (2026-11-24, verbatim in D-099): 「Ok Dag 也要允許群組順序改動」. Read D-096, D-098 and D-099 first, and the `actl dag` code from #125 (devloop/dag_edit.py, devloop/core/dagedit.py) and #122 (devloop/core/chain.py). Tests go in tests_devloop/test_dag_edit.py and tests_devloop/test_chain.py using loop_harness.py; each case runs in seconds.

Why: in T (2026-11-24) groups g63, g70 and g78 had all their tickets merged into their int branches, so `actl dag dep` and `actl dag move` refused them (frozen, D-089), and the main session could not put them after the group of #320 as the owner wanted. The chain order comes only from ticket dependencies and creation order, so there was no way to say "this group after that one".

Wanted:
1. A group-order edge kept in dag.json (a new field, e.g. `group_after: {"g63": ["g88"]}`), written only through the pool's validated write. core/chain.py builds the group graph from ticket dependencies plus these edges; the chain is a topological order of that graph with today's tie-break (created, then id).
2. `actl dag after gA --add gB --reason "..."` puts group A after group B; `actl dag after gA --drop gB --reason "..."` removes an edge added this way (ticket dependencies are not touched). `--by` as the other `actl dag` commands (default main-session). The last stdout line is the chain after the change, like the other dag commands.
3. Refused with one line, nothing written: A or B does not exist; A == B; A has started or finished its regression (a regression job running, or state verified, landed or cancelled); B is landed or cancelled (adding is pointless; dropping an existing edge to a landed B is allowed); the edge makes a cycle with the ticket dependencies or other edges; `--drop` of an edge that is not there. A group whose tickets are merged (state pr, or open with merged members) can be reordered: that is the point.
4. Each change writes an event on both groups (who, why). When a group is moved behind another, nothing else changes now: when the earlier group lands, follow_main brings main into the later group's branch as today, and its regression runs after that (D-098).
5. Edges to a group that lands or is cancelled stay in dag.json as history but no longer constrain the order. Pool validation refuses a dag.json whose group edges make a cycle.
6. The board's DAG view and the idle/chain pages show the order as computed (no board action to change it, D-096). Document `actl dag after` in devloop/README.md next to `actl dag dep/move`, and add one line to CLAUDE.md 「怎麼做事」 after the `actl dag move` line: 「把整組排到另一組後面是 `actl dag after gA --add gB --reason "…"`(票已合入的組也可以)」.
- removes: the main session's inability to set the order of groups whose tickets are merged.
- Out of scope: the board offering this action; reordering a group that has started its regression.
